mechanisms.name: Storefront `configuration-snippet` vs. the new security defaults ("Enable security features by default (#11819)": `--enable-annotation-validation` on by default, `annotations-risk-level` lowered to "High")
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: One breaking change very likely affects this environment
resourcesConsumers: admission webhook (failurePolicy: Fail on Ingress CREATE and UPDATE)
PCI-required HSTS and X-Frame-Options: DENY headers
mechanisms.mechanism: v1.12.0 changes the default `annotations-risk-level` to `High`, and snippet annotations are classified Critical, so the High level excludes them regardless of `allow-snippet-annotations: true` (which only gates whether snippets are permitted at all). The assessment expects the controller to reject or ignore the annotation. The change is a binary default, not a manifest change, so the unchanged rendered manifest does not show unchanged behavior. Likely consequences: the webhook could reject a sync of the storefront Ingress, including an Argo self-heal. When new pods start they re-evaluate the existing Ingress, so the storefront host may lose its configuration or only the security headers. That would be a PCI regression and possibly an outage. Argo CD sync would show errors or drift, though the controller rollout itself can still succeed.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: No current mitigation: `allowSnippetAnnotations: true` does not prevent it. Fix options for the owner to decide (the first is a security-owner decision because of PCI): set `controller.config.annotations-risk-level: Critical`, which keeps the snippet working and keeps snippets enabled; or replace the snippet with `add-headers` / `custom-headers` (ConfigMap-based) or `more_set_headers` in a controller-level `server-snippet` / `location-snippet`, which needs its own review.
citedEvidence: env/apps/storefront/overlays/prod/ingress-headers.yaml sets nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet (HSTS, X-Frame-Options: DENY); its file comment says the PCI review requires these headers
rendered ConfigMap carries allow-snippet-annotations: "true" in both versions
rendered/manifest.diff shows no ConfigMap change and no --enable-annotation-validation arg in either version
chart value enableAnnotationValidations false (4.11.5, line 20) to true (4.12.0, line 24), with no visible arg in the render
assumptions: The conclusion is inferred from upstream behavior the author knows of. It is not proven by the files supplied.
Snippet annotations are classified Critical (to be confirmed).
The existing Ingress is re-evaluated when the new controller pods start.
missingEvidence: Upstream annotation docs and annotations-risk-level ConfigMap docs are not in upstream/
Controller source is not in the provided files
No staging run: Bash was denied, so the author could not run anything
Only prod is covered by the renders
recommendedValidation: Staging test of the storefront Ingress on 1.12.0 with production values: check that the webhook admits it, inspect the generated nginx config for shop.example.com, confirm curl -I returns HSTS and X-Frame-Options; repeat after a controller pod restart
Confirm the exact risk classification of configuration-snippet and the behavior of existing Ingresses in 1.12.0
Check staging 1.12.0 controller logs for "risky annotation" or validation messages
Decide the header strategy with the security/PCI owner
Check the other shop clusters that share values.yaml
Change the chart version and the risk-level setting together in one PR and keep a rollback path (revert targetRevision to 4.11.5)
Watch the first Argo sync closely (selfHeal/prune on, webhook failurePolicy: Fail)
